tool.name: ChIP-seq reproducibility
tool.description: with true, pooled and self pseudoreplicate IDR
tool.command: bash '$__tool_directory__/run_idr_pipeline.sh' --sample idr --output-dir output --treatment-bam '$treatment_1' --control-bam '$control_1' --treatment-bam '$treatment_2' --control-bam '$control_2' --replicate-label rep1 --replicate-label rep2 --format '$macs_options.input_format' --genome-size '$macs_options.genome_size' --bandwidth '$macs_options.bandwidth' --mfold-low '$macs_options.mfold_low' --mfold-high '$macs_options.mfold_high' --$macs_options.cutoff.kind '$macs_options.cutoff.value' --rank '$idr_options.rank' --idr-threshold '${"%.12f" % float($idr_options.threshold)}' --threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} --seed '$idr_options.seed' --macs2-extra-arg '--keep-dup' --macs2-extra-arg '$macs_options.keep_dup' #if $macs_options.nomodel --macs2-extra-arg '--nomodel' #end if #if $peak_input.mode == 'existing' --narrowpeak '$peak_input.peak_1' --narrowpeak '$peak_input.peak_2' #end if > '$pipeline_log' 2>&1

param.name: peak_1
param.label: narrowPeak — biological replicate 1
param.help: MACS2 narrowPeak file with ten columns, represented as BED in Galaxy.

param.name: peak_2
param.label: narrowPeak — biological replicate 2
param.help: MACS2 narrowPeak file with ten columns, represented as BED in Galaxy.

param.name: genome_size
param.label: Effective genome size
param.help: Positive number of effectively mappable bases, for example 1.87e9; choose a value appropriate for your organism.

validator.message: Enter a positive number, optionally in scientific notation.

param.name: mfold_high
param.label: Upper model fold-enrichment bound
param.help: Must be greater than the lower bound. Model parameters are not used in BAMPE mode.

param.name: nomodel
param.label: Skip fragment-size model building
param.help: Relevant to single-end data; BAMPE uses observed fragment lengths.

param.name: keep_dup
param.label: MACS2 duplicate handling
param.help: Applied independently in each peak-calling run. Choose consistently with BAM preprocessing and with any supplied narrowPeak files.
param.option: Keep at most one fragment/tag per identical position (MACS2 default)

param.name: threshold
param.label: Global IDR threshold
param.help: Only peaks passing this threshold are reported and counted.

param.name: seed
param.label: Pseudoreplicate assignment seed
param.help: The scripts derive additional seeds for controls and the second biological replicate.

tool.help:
Evaluate ChIP-seq reproducibility for two biological replicates ================================================================
Provide two ChIP BAM files and their matched control BAM files. Choose BAMPE for paired-end data and BAM for single-end data. All files must refer to the same reference genome. In the accompanying PP script, pooled BAMs are concatenated after sequence-dictionary checks; coordinate sorting is not required. Pseudoreplicate assignment keeps the mates of each template together and produces approximately equal complementary halves.
The tool executes:
* **TR:** IDR between the two biological replicates (Nt). * **PP:** IDR between the two pooled pseudoreplicates (Np). * **SP:** IDR between the two self pseudoreplicates of each biological replicate (N1 and N2).
Existing narrowPeak files can replace peak calling in TR only. They must be in replicate order and have been generated using the same peak-calling parameters and preprocessing strategy as those selected here. BAM files remain required for PP and SP.
The summary reports rescue_ratio = max(Nt, Np) / min(Nt, Np) and self_consistency_ratio = max(N1, N2) / min(N1, N2). A ratio is reported as NA when either corresponding count is zero. Counts include only peaks passing the selected global IDR threshold.
IDR peak outputs use the tabular datatype because IDR adds columns to the standard narrowPeak fields. MACS2 narrowPeak files use the BED datatype in Galaxy. The narrowPeak collection contains the MACS2 peaks generated by this run: eight files in BAM-only mode, six when existing peaks are supplied. The supplied TR peaks remain in the history and are not copied into this collection.
The branch manifest contains paths inside the job working directory; use the separate Galaxy output datasets to access those results after the job ends. The internal sample name is fixed to idr and replicate labels to rep1/rep2. Output labels identify the Galaxy input datasets.
CPU allocation is obtained from GALAXY_SLOTS. MACS2 calls and branches currently run sequentially; the thread allocation applies to samtools.
